effects.story: A $10 discount causally changes purchase probability by +10.9 pts (95% CI +9.1 pts to +12.7 pts). A naive before/after comparison (+6.0 pts) under-estimates the effect by 44% because historical targeting sent bigger discounts to customers who were already unlikely to buy. Ground truth for this simulation is +10.0 pts.

A $20 discount causally changes purchase probability by +17.8 pts (95% CI +15.2 pts to +20.4 pts). A naive before/after comparison (+6.0 pts) under-estimates the effect by 66% because historical targeting sent bigger discounts to customers who were already unlikely to buy. Ground truth for this simulation is +16.4 pts.

narrative: With a $5,000 budget the causal optimiser targets 1,597 customers (1,590 × $10, 7 × $20) for an expected $4,863 incremental profit.
This strategy earns $7,220 more than blanket $10 targeting with the same budget.
This strategy earns $9,600 more than the traditional purchase-propensity model with the same budget.
The traditional model would spend $1,838 on customers who would have bought anyway or do not respond, versus $35 for the causal optimiser.
10% of customers are Sure Things – they buy without a coupon, so they are excluded.
10% are Sleeping Dogs whose purchase probability drops when offered a discount.
